text:
Credit Scores and Credit Bureaus in India (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of how credit information companies work in India under the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005 and RBI directions, including the RBI compensation framework for credit information complaints (circular of 26 October 2023). General information, not financial advice. Last reviewed: October 2026.

Credit Scores and Credit Bureaus in India (Public Information) — The Four Credit Bureaus

India has four RBI-licensed credit information companies (CICs), also called credit bureaus: TransUnion CIBIL, Experian, Equifax and CRIF High Mark. Banks report every borrower's loan and credit card repayment history to them, and check them before approving a new loan.

Credit Scores and Credit Bureaus in India (Public Information) — Credit Score

A credit score is a three-digit number, usually between 300 and 900, that summarises how reliably a person has repaid credit. Many lenders prefer a score of around 700–750 or above. The main factors are paying EMIs and card bills on time, how much of the available credit limit is used, the length of credit history, the mix of secured and unsecured loans, and how many new loans or cards were applied for recently.

Credit Scores and Credit Bureaus in India (Public Information) — Free Credit Report

Every person is entitled to one free full credit report, including the credit score, once a year from each of the four credit bureaus. It can be requested on each bureau's official website. Checking your own report does not lower your score.

Credit Scores and Credit Bureaus in India (Public Information) — Fixing Errors

If a credit report has a mistake, such as a loan shown as unpaid after it was closed, raise a dispute with the credit bureau or the lender. The lender has 21 days and the bureau 9 days — 30 days in total — to resolve it. If it is not resolved within 30 days, the customer is entitled to compensation of ₹100 for each day of delay.

Credit Scores and Credit Bureaus in India (Public Information) — Alerts and Default Reporting

Banks must inform a borrower before reporting a default to the credit bureaus, and credit bureaus send SMS or email alerts when a customer's credit report is accessed by a lender.

Credit Scores and Credit Bureaus in India (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**Will one late EMI affect my credit score?**
Yes, any EMI reported as overdue (even in the SMA-0 stage of up to 30 days) can lower the score. Paying as soon as possible and keeping later payments on time helps it recover.

**Does closing a loan early hurt my credit score?**
No. A loan closed in full is reported as closed and generally does not hurt the score.

Banking Fraud Safety and Genuine Bank Calls (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of RBI guidance on customer protection in unauthorised electronic transactions (circular of 6 July 2017), the RBI circular on use of 1600xx and 140xx numbers for bank calls (17 January 2025), and Government of India cyber-fraud reporting channels. General information, not legal advice. Last reviewed: October 2026.

Banking Fraud Safety and Genuine Bank Calls (Public Information) — What a Bank Will Never Ask For

A genuine bank, its staff, or its voice assistant will never ask for an OTP, UPI PIN, ATM PIN, CVV, net-banking password, or full card number — not on a call, SMS, email, WhatsApp or link. A genuine bank will also never ask a customer to install a screen-sharing or remote-access app, or to "verify KYC" by clicking a link.

metadata.section: What a Bank Will Never Ask For

text:
Banking Fraud Safety and Genuine Bank Calls (Public Information) — How to Recognise a Genuine Bank Call

Under RBI's January 2025 instructions, banks are to use numbers starting with 1600 for service and transaction-related calls, and numbers starting with 140 for promotional calls. Calls about your account from ordinary 10-digit mobile numbers should be treated with suspicion. When in doubt, hang up and call the number printed on the back of your card or on the bank's official website.

metadata.section: How to Recognise a Genuine Bank Call

text:
Banking Fraud Safety and Genuine Bank Calls (Public Information) — If You Are a Victim of Fraud

Act immediately: call the national cyber fraud helpline 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in, and inform your bank so it can block the card or account. Suspected fraud calls and messages, even if no money was lost, can be reported through Chakshu on the Sanchar Saathi portal.

metadata.section: If You Are a Victim of Fraud

text:
Banking Fraud Safety and Genuine Bank Calls (Public Information) — Your Liability for Unauthorised Transactions

Under RBI rules, if an unauthorised electronic transaction happened because of a fault at the bank's end, or a third-party breach that the customer reports within 3 working days, the customer has zero liability. If reported within 4 to 7 working days, the customer's liability is limited to the transaction amount or a cap of ₹5,000 to ₹25,000 depending on the account type, whichever is lower. The bank must credit the disputed amount (shadow reversal) within 10 working days of being informed.

Banking Fraud Safety and Genuine Bank Calls (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**Someone from "the bank" said my loan EMI bounced and I must pay through a link. Is it real?**
Treat it as suspicious. Pay only through your bank's official app, website, branch or auto-debit — never through a link sent by an unknown caller.

**I shared my OTP by mistake. What now?**
Call your bank right away to block the card or account, then call 1930 and report at cybercrime.gov.in. Reporting within 3 working days protects your rights under RBI rules.

Complaints, Grievance Redressal and the RBI Ombudsman (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of the Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026 (effective 1 July 2026, replacing the 2021 scheme). Applies to all banks and RBI-regulated entities. General information, not legal advice — check rbi.org.in and cms.rbi.org.in for the current text. Last reviewed: October 2026.

Complaints, Grievance Redressal and the RBI Ombudsman (Public Information) — Step 1 — Complain to the Bank First

A complaint must first be made to the bank itself — at a branch, through its customer care, website or app, or to its grievance redressal or nodal officer, whose contact details every bank must publish. The bank should acknowledge the complaint and give a reference number. Banks generally have up to 30 days to resolve a complaint.

metadata.section: Step 1 — Complain to the Bank First

text:
Complaints, Grievance Redressal and the RBI Ombudsman (Public Information) — Step 2 — RBI Ombudsman

If the bank rejects the complaint, does not reply within the allowed time, or the customer is not satisfied with the reply, the customer can complain to the RBI Ombudsman. Under the 2026 scheme the complaint must be filed within 90 days from the end of the bank's response period or from the bank's last reply, whichever is later. Filing is free and does not need a lawyer.

Complaints, Grievance Redressal and the RBI Ombudsman (Public Information) — How to File

Online at the RBI Complaint Management System (cms.rbi.org.in), by email, or by post to the RBI's Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre. The RBI's toll-free contact centre number is 14448, which also helps with filing and tracking complaints.

Complaints, Grievance Redressal and the RBI Ombudsman (Public Information) — Compensation

The Ombudsman can award compensation of up to ₹30 lakh for the actual financial loss suffered, plus up to ₹3 lakh for the customer's loss of time, expenses, harassment and mental anguish. There is no limit on the amount in dispute that can be complained about.

Complaints, Grievance Redressal and the RBI Ombudsman (Public Information) — What the Ombudsman Does Not Handle

Commercial decisions of the bank (such as whether to approve a loan or the interest rate it offers, unless a regulation is broken), matters already before a court or another forum, and disputes about services outside the RBI's purview. Either side can appeal an Ombudsman's decision to the Appellate Authority within 30 days.

metadata.section: What the Ombudsman Does Not Handle

text:
Complaints, Grievance Redressal and the RBI Ombudsman (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**My bank hasn't returned my property papers two months after I closed my loan. Can I complain?**
Yes. Complain to the bank first; if it is not resolved, the RBI Ombudsman can take it up. RBI rules also require the bank to pay ₹5,000 per day of delay beyond 30 days.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — EMI FAQ — Overview

> This is fictional demo FAQ content for "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. For a specific customer's actual EMI amount, outstanding balance, or due date, LoanMate looks up the real value from the customer's account rather than relying on this general document.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — EMI FAQ — Section: What Is an EMI

An EMI (Equated Monthly Instalment) is the fixed monthly payment a borrower makes towards a loan, covering both a portion of the principal and the interest for that month, calculated using a standard reducing-balance formula.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — EMI FAQ — Section: Payment Methods

**How can I make my EMI payment?**
EMIs are collected via ECS (auto-debit) from the customer's registered bank account on the due date. Payments can also be made through net banking, UPI, or at a branch.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — EMI FAQ — Section: Changing Your EMI

**Can I change my EMI due date?**
LoanMate's demo policy allows a one-time change of EMI due date per loan, subject to the new date being within the same billing cycle window. This would need to be requested through a branch or the customer support team, not through this voice assistant.

**Can I reduce my EMI amount?**
An EMI amount can be reduced either by making a prepayment (see the Prepayment Policy) or by extending the loan's remaining tenure, which increases total interest paid over the life of the loan.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — EMI FAQ — Section: Understanding Your EMI Breakdown

Each EMI is split into a principal component and an interest component. In the early part of a loan's tenure, a larger share of each EMI goes towards interest; as the loan matures, a larger share goes towards principal. This is standard for reducing-balance loans and is not specific to any one LoanMate product.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — General Banking FAQ — Overview

> This is fictional demo FAQ content for "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — General Banking FAQ — Section: About LoanMate

**What is LoanMate?**
LoanMate is a demo conversational voice assistant that helps customers of a fictional bank get information about their loans and ask general loan-related questions, in English, Hindi, or Hinglish.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — General Banking FAQ — Section: Talking to a Human

**Can I speak to a real person?**
Yes. If you ask to speak with a human agent, a loan officer, or customer care, LoanMate will acknowledge the request and let you know it will be flagged for follow-up. In this demo, no real human agent is actually connected.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — General Banking FAQ — Section: Calling LoanMate vs LoanMate Calling You

**What can I do when I call LoanMate?**
When you call, LoanMate is your service desk: ask about your EMI, balance, due date or loan status, ask about products and policies, or request a service — an account statement, a no-dues certificate, a foreclosure quote, an interest certificate, a complaint, or a callback from a human officer. Every request gets a reference number.

**Why would LoanMate call me?**
LoanMate calls only for a specific reason: a reminder about an upcoming EMI, a follow-up on an overdue payment, a pending KYC update, or a product update such as a top-up loan offer. It will first confirm it is speaking to the right person before sharing any account details, and it will respect a request to call back later or not to call again.

**Will LoanMate ask for my OTP or PIN?**
Never. Neither LoanMate nor any genuine bank asks for an OTP, PIN, CVV or password on a call.

Personal Loans are unsecured (no collateral). Home Loans are secured by the property being financed. Vehicle Loans are secured by the vehicle. Education Loans above ₹7.5 lakhs generally require collateral. Business Loans up to ₹50 lakhs may be unsecured for eligible businesses.

Government Education Loan Schemes (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) Model Education Loan Scheme and Ministry of Education schemes — PM-Vidyalaxmi (approved November 2024), Central Sector Interest Subsidy (CSIS) and the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Education Loans (CGFSEL). General information — check pmvidyalaxmi.co.in and the lender for current terms. Last reviewed: October 2026.

Government Education Loan Schemes (Public Information) — IBA Model Education Loan Scheme

Most banks follow the IBA model scheme for education loans in India and abroad. The repayment holiday (moratorium) is the course period plus one year. Repayment can then be spread over up to 15 years. For loans up to ₹4 lakh no margin money is usually needed, and loans up to ₹7.5 lakh are generally given without collateral, backed by a government credit guarantee.

Government Education Loan Schemes (Public Information) — PM-Vidyalaxmi

PM-Vidyalaxmi offers collateral-free and guarantor-free education loans to students admitted to quality higher education institutions (based on national NIRF rankings). For loans up to ₹7.5 lakh, the Government guarantees 75% of any default to the bank. Students with family income up to ₹8 lakh a year, not covered by other schemes, get 3% interest subvention during the moratorium on loans up to ₹10 lakh. Applications are made on the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal.

Government Education Loan Schemes (Public Information) — Central Sector Interest Subsidy (CSIS)

Students from families with annual income up to ₹4.5 lakh can get full interest subsidy during the moratorium period on education loans up to ₹10 lakh taken under the IBA model scheme for recognised courses in India. This is in addition to the PM-Vidyalaxmi 3% subvention for the ₹4.5–8 lakh income band.

Government Education Loan Schemes (Public Information) — Tax Benefit on Education Loan Interest

Under the old income-tax regime, the full interest paid on an education loan for higher studies of yourself, your spouse or children can be deducted (Section 80E of the Income-tax Act, 1961), with no upper limit, for up to 8 years from the year repayment starts. See the loan tax benefits document for details.

metadata.section: Tax Benefit on Education Loan Interest

text:
Government Education Loan Schemes (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**Do I need collateral for a ₹6 lakh education loan?**
Usually not — loans up to ₹7.5 lakh are generally collateral-free under the IBA model scheme and the government credit guarantee, though the bank may still ask for a parent or guardian as co-borrower.

Income Tax Benefits on Loans in India (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of income-tax deductions on loans. Section numbers refer to the Income-tax Act, 1961; the Income-tax Act, 2025, which applies from 1 April 2026, renumbers these provisions. General information, not tax advice — consult a tax professional for your situation. Last reviewed: October 2026.

Income Tax Benefits on Loans in India (Public Information) — Old vs New Tax Regime

Most loan-related deductions are available only under the old tax regime. The new tax regime, which is the default, has lower tax rates but does not allow the principal deduction (Section 80C), the self-occupied home loan interest deduction, or the education loan interest deduction (Section 80E). A taxpayer can compare both and choose.

Income Tax Benefits on Loans in India (Public Information) — Home Loan

Under the old regime: principal repaid on a home loan can be claimed under Section 80C, within the overall ₹1.5 lakh limit (shared with PPF, ELSS, life insurance, etc.); interest paid on a loan for a self-occupied house can be deducted up to ₹2 lakh a year under Section 24(b). For a let-out property, interest is deductible against rental income under both regimes, but the loss that can be set off against other income is limited. Joint home-loan borrowers who are also co-owners can each claim these deductions separately.

Income Tax Benefits on Loans in India (Public Information) — Education Loan

Under the old regime, the entire interest paid on an education loan from a bank or approved institution — for higher studies of yourself, your spouse, your children, or a student you are the legal guardian of — is deductible under Section 80E, with no upper limit. The deduction is available for up to 8 years, starting from the year repayment begins. The principal repaid is not deductible.

Income Tax Benefits on Loans in India (Public Information) — Personal, Car and Gold Loans

There is generally no tax deduction for personal, car or gold loans used for personal purposes. If the money is used for business, or to buy, build or renovate a house, the interest may be deductible under the relevant business or house-property rules, with supporting proof.

Income Tax Benefits on Loans in India (Public Information) — Interest Certificate

To claim home or education loan deductions, ask the bank for an interest certificate (a provisional certificate during the year and a final certificate after 31 March) showing the principal and interest paid.

PMAY-Urban 2.0 Home Loan Interest Subsidy (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of the Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS) under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0, run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India. Source: pmaymis.gov.in. General information — eligibility is decided by the lender and the scheme's nodal agencies. Last reviewed: October 2026.

PMAY-Urban 2.0 Home Loan Interest Subsidy (Public Information) — What the Scheme Offers

PMAY-U 2.0's Interest Subsidy Scheme gives first-time home buyers in urban areas from lower- and middle-income families a government subsidy on home loan interest. It applies to home loans sanctioned and disbursed on or after 1 September 2024.

PMAY-Urban 2.0 Home Loan Interest Subsidy (Public Information) — Subsidy Amount

The subsidy is 4% interest on the first ₹8 lakh of the home loan, calculated over up to 12 years, with a maximum benefit of ₹1.80 lakh. The loan itself can be larger than ₹8 lakh, but the subsidy is calculated only on the first ₹8 lakh. The subsidy is released to the borrower's loan account in up to five yearly instalments.

PMAY-Urban 2.0 Home Loan Interest Subsidy (Public Information) — Who Is Eligible

Families in the Economically Weaker Section (annual household income up to ₹3 lakh), Low Income Group (₹3 lakh to ₹6 lakh) and Middle Income Group (₹6 lakh to ₹9 lakh). The family must not own a pucca house anywhere in India. The home loan must be up to ₹25 lakh, for a house worth up to ₹35 lakh, with a carpet area up to 120 square metres.

PMAY-Urban 2.0 Home Loan Interest Subsidy (Public Information) — How to Apply

Apply on the PMAY-U 2.0 portal (pmaymis.gov.in) or through a participating bank or housing finance company when taking the home loan. The loan account must stay regular for the instalments to be released.

PMAY-Urban 2.0 Home Loan Interest Subsidy (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**I earn ₹8 lakh a year and am buying my first flat for ₹30 lakh with a ₹20 lakh loan. Could I be eligible?**
Your income falls in the Middle Income Group and the loan and property values are within limits, so you may be eligible, subject to the scheme's other conditions and the lender's checks.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Business Loan — Overview

> This is a fictional demo product of "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. It does not describe a real bank's policy. Figures are in line with typical ranges at Indian banks; government scheme details are public information.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Business Loan — Overview

The LoanMate Business Loan funds working capital, equipment purchase, inventory or expansion for self-employed professionals, proprietors, partnerships and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Business Loan — Interest Rate, Amount and Tenure

Unsecured business loans carry an interest rate of 11% to 18% per annum, for amounts from ₹1 lakh to ₹50 lakh and a tenure of 1 to 5 years. Secured business loans and loans against property are available at lower rates for larger amounts.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Business Loan — Charges

A processing fee of up to 2% of the loan amount plus GST. Under RBI's 2025 prepayment directions, floating-rate business loans taken by individuals and micro and small enterprises from commercial banks carry no prepayment charges; fixed-rate business loans may carry a prepayment charge of 2% to 4% of the outstanding principal, as disclosed in the Key Fact Statement.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Business Loan — Eligibility and Documents

Business running for at least 2 years, with a minimum annual turnover of ₹10 lakh and a credit score of 700 or above preferred. Documents: KYC of the business and owners, business registration (GST certificate, Udyam registration or trade licence), the last 2 years' IT returns with audited financials, and the last 12 months' bank statements.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Business Loan — Government-Backed Options

Micro and small enterprises can get collateral-free loans under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), where the government trust guarantees a share of the loan. Small businesses can also apply for Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) loans for non-farm income-generating activities through banks.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Business Loan — Frequently Asked Questions

**What happens if my business loan becomes overdue?**
The same RBI rules apply as for other loans: overdue accounts are reported as SMA and, after 90 days overdue, classified as NPA. Talk to the bank early about rescheduling if cash flow is tight.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Car Loan — Overview

> This is a fictional demo product of "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. It does not describe a real bank's policy. Figures are in line with typical ranges at Indian banks.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Car Loan — Overview

The LoanMate Car Loan finances the purchase of a new car, or a used car up to 5 years old. The car is hypothecated to the bank — the bank's interest is recorded on the registration certificate (RC) until the loan is fully repaid.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Car Loan — Interest Rate

New car loans carry an interest rate of 8.75% to 12% per annum, and used car loans 11% to 15% per annum, depending on the customer's credit score and income. Car loans are usually on a fixed rate.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Car Loan — Loan Amount and Tenure

Up to 90% of the on-road price for new cars and up to 80% of the valuation for used cars. The repayment tenure is 1 to 7 years for new cars and up to 5 years for used cars.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Car Loan — Charges

A processing fee of up to 1% of the loan amount plus GST. Fixed-rate car loans carry a prepayment or foreclosure charge of up to 5% of the outstanding principal if closed within the first 12 months and up to 3% after that, as stated in the Key Fact Statement.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Car Loan — Eligibility and Documents

Age 21 to 65 years, minimum income of ₹25,000 per month (salaried) or ₹3 lakh per year (self-employed), and a credit score of 700 or above preferred. Documents: KYC, the latest 3 months' salary slips or 2 years' IT returns, the last 6 months' bank statements, and the car's pro-forma invoice.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Car Loan — After Closing the Loan

Once the loan is repaid, LoanMate issues a no-objection certificate (NOC) and Form 35 so the hypothecation can be removed from the RC at the RTO. Under RBI rules, original documents must be returned within 30 days of closure.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Car Loan — Frequently Asked Questions

**Can I sell my car before the loan is closed?**
Only after closing the loan or with the bank's consent, because the car is hypothecated to the bank.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Education Loan — Overview

> This is a fictional demo product of "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. It does not describe a real bank's policy.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Education Loan — Overview

The LoanMate Education Loan funds higher education in India or abroad, covering tuition, living expenses, and related academic costs.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Education Loan — Interest Rate

LoanMate Education Loans carry an interest rate of 9% to 13% per annum.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Education Loan — Loan Amount and Tenure

Up to ₹1,50,00,000 for study in India, and up to ₹2,00,00,000 for study abroad. The repayment tenure is up to 15 years.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Education Loan — Moratorium Period

Repayment is not required during the course duration plus an additional 12 months after course completion. This is known as the moratorium period.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Education Loan — Processing Fee

No processing fee for loans up to ₹10 lakhs. A 1% processing fee applies above that amount.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Education Loan — Eligibility Criteria

- Applicant must be a student admitted to a recognised institution
- A parent or guardian is required as a co-applicant
- Covers graduate, post-graduate, professional, and vocational courses

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Education Loan — Required Documents

- KYC documents of both the student and the co-applicant
- Admission letter from the institution
- Fee structure or fee schedule
- Academic records (mark sheets, certificates)
- Income proof of the co-applicant
- Collateral documents, required for loans above ₹7.5 lakhs

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Education Loan — Frequently Asked Questions

**When does repayment start?**
Repayment begins after the moratorium period ends — that is, course completion plus 12 months, or 6 months after the student starts a job, whichever comes first.

**Is there a tax benefit?**
Interest paid on education loans is generally deductible under Section 80E of the Indian Income Tax Act for up to 8 years. This is general information, not tax advice.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Gold Loan — Overview

> This is a fictional demo product of "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. The interest rate and charges are demo values; the loan-to-value and gold-return rules summarise the public RBI (Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral) Directions, 2025, which apply from 1 April 2026.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Gold Loan — Overview

The LoanMate Gold Loan is a secured loan against gold jewellery or coins. It is quick to sanction, needs little documentation, and the gold is kept in the bank's secure custody until the loan is repaid.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Gold Loan — Interest Rate and Tenure

In this demo policy, gold loans carry an interest rate of 8.5% to 14% per annum, for a tenure of up to 12 months. Customers can pay a regular EMI, pay interest monthly and the principal at the end, or repay everything in one bullet payment at the end of the tenure.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Gold Loan — Loan-to-Value (LTV) — RBI Limits

Under the RBI's 2025 gold-loan directions, for consumption loans the bank can lend up to 85% of the gold's value for loans up to ₹2.5 lakh, up to 80% for loans above ₹2.5 lakh and up to ₹5 lakh, and up to 75% for larger loans. For bullet-repayment loans, the interest due over the tenure is counted within this limit. Gold is valued at the average closing price of 22-carat gold of the previous 30 days or the previous day, whichever is lower; stones and other metals are not counted.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Gold Loan — Documents

KYC documents only. For small loans, if the customer does not have the original purchase receipt, a self-declaration of ownership is accepted. Gold bars and gold ETFs are not accepted as collateral.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Gold Loan — Return of Gold

After the loan is fully repaid, the gold must be returned within 7 working days. Under the RBI directions, if the delay is the bank's fault, the bank pays ₹5,000 per day of delay. If the loan is not repaid, the bank may auction the gold only after giving the borrower prior notice, and must return any surplus after recovering its dues.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Gold Loan — Frequently Asked Questions

**How much can I get on 20 grams of gold?**
It depends on the gold's purity and current price. For a loan up to ₹2.5 lakh, the bank can lend up to 85% of the gold's assessed value.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Home Loan — Overview

> This is a fictional demo product of "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. It does not describe a real bank's policy.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Home Loan — Overview

The LoanMate Home Loan finances the purchase, construction, or renovation of a residential property. Both floating and fixed interest rate options are available.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Home Loan — Interest Rate

LoanMate Home Loans carry an interest rate of 8.25% to 10.5% per annum.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Home Loan — Loan Amount and Tenure

The loan amount ranges from ₹5,00,000 to ₹10,00,00,000. The repayment tenure ranges from 5 to 30 years.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Home Loan — Processing Fee

A processing fee of 0.5% to 1% of the loan amount, plus applicable GST, is charged at disbursement.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Home Loan — Loan-to-Value (LTV) Ratio

LoanMate finances up to 90% of the property value for loans up to ₹30 lakhs, and up to 80% of the property value for higher loan amounts.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Home Loan — Eligibility Criteria

- Age: 21 to 65 years (at loan maturity)
- Employment: Salaried, self-employed, or NRI applicants
- Minimum income (salaried): ₹30,000 per month
- Credit score: 675 and above
- Property must be in an approved location or a RERA-registered project

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Home Loan — Required Documents

- KYC documents (Aadhaar / PAN / Passport)
- Last 3 months' salary slips (salaried applicants)
- Last 2 years' IT returns
- Last 6 months' bank statements
- Property documents (sale deed, allotment letter, or approved building plan)
- No-objection certificate (NOC) from the builder or housing society

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Home Loan — Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the maximum LTV ratio?**
Up to 90% of property value for loans up to ₹30 lakhs, and up to 75–80% for higher loan amounts.

**Can I apply jointly for a home loan?**
Yes. Joint applications with a co-applicant, such as a spouse or parent, are allowed and may improve loan eligibility.

**Is there a tax benefit on home loans?**
Yes, under Indian income tax law generally: principal repayment (Section 80C, up to ₹1.5 lakh) and interest paid (Section 24(b), up to ₹2 lakh). This is general information, not tax advice — please consult a tax professional for your specific situation.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Personal Loan — Overview

> This is a fictional demo product of "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. It does not describe a real bank's policy.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Personal Loan — Overview

The LoanMate Personal Loan is an unsecured loan for personal financial needs such as medical expenses, travel, wedding costs, or home renovation. No collateral or guarantor is required.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Personal Loan — Interest Rate

LoanMate Personal Loans carry an interest rate of 10.5% to 16% per annum, depending on the applicant's credit score, income, and existing obligations.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Personal Loan — Loan Amount and Tenure

The loan amount ranges from ₹50,000 to ₹40,00,000. The repayment tenure ranges from 12 to 60 months.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Personal Loan — Processing Fee

A processing fee of up to 2% of the loan amount, plus applicable GST, is charged at disbursement.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Personal Loan — Eligibility Criteria

- Age: 21 to 60 years
- Employment: Salaried or self-employed professionals
- Minimum income (salaried): ₹25,000 per month
- Minimum income (self-employed): ₹3,00,000 per year
- Credit score: 700 and above preferred
- Work experience: Minimum 2 years, with at least 1 year in the current job (for salaried applicants)

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Personal Loan — Required Documents — Salaried Applicants

- KYC documents (Aadhaar / PAN / Passport / Voter ID)
- Last 3 months' salary slips
- Last 6 months' bank statements
- Form 16 or IT returns for the last 2 years
- Employment certificate or offer letter

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Personal Loan — Required Documents — Self-Employed Applicants

- KYC documents (Aadhaar / PAN)
- Last 2 years' IT returns with computation
- Last 6 months' bank statements
- Business proof (GST registration / trade licence)
- Certified financials (profit & loss statement, balance sheet)

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Personal Loan — Frequently Asked Questions

**Can I get a personal loan without collateral?**
Yes. LoanMate Personal Loans are unsecured — no collateral or guarantor is required.

**How quickly is the loan disbursed?**
For eligible applicants with complete documentation, disbursal can happen within 24–48 hours.

**Can I prepay my personal loan?**
Yes. Prepayment is allowed after 12 EMIs. See the LoanMate Prepayment Policy for charges that may apply.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Top-up Loan — Overview

> This is a fictional demo product of "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. It does not describe a real bank's policy. Its design follows how top-up loans commonly work at Indian banks.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Top-up Loan — Overview

A LoanMate Top-up Loan gives existing borrowers additional funds on top of their current home, car or personal loan, without a fresh application from scratch. The top-up runs alongside the existing loan with its own EMI. It can be used for any genuine personal need — home renovation, education, medical expenses, a wedding, or consolidating costlier debt — but not for speculative purposes such as trading in shares.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Top-up Loan — Who Can Get a Top-up

Existing LoanMate borrowers whose loan is active and has a clean repayment record: at least 12 EMIs paid on time for a home loan, or at least 6 EMIs paid on time for a car or personal loan, with no EMI currently overdue. Final eligibility depends on the customer's income, credit score and, for home loans, the current property value. Being offered a top-up on a call is not an approval.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Top-up Loan — Interest Rate and Amount

In this demo policy, a home-loan top-up is priced 0.25% to 1% above the customer's existing home loan rate, and a car or personal loan top-up at the bank's prevailing personal loan rate of 10.5% to 16% per annum. For a home loan, the existing loan plus the top-up cannot exceed the RBI's loan-to-value limits on the property's current value. Personal and car loan top-ups range from ₹50,000 to ₹10 lakh.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Top-up Loan — Tenure and Charges

A home-loan top-up can run up to the remaining tenure of the home loan, to a maximum of 15 years. Car and personal loan top-ups run up to 5 years. A processing fee of up to 1% of the top-up amount plus GST applies. Floating-rate top-ups taken by individuals carry no prepayment charges, as per RBI rules.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Top-up Loan — Documents

Usually only updated KYC, the latest 3 months' salary slips or latest income proof, and the last 6 months' bank statements. Property documents are already held for the existing home loan.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Top-up Loan — Frequently Asked Questions

**Is a top-up cheaper than a personal loan?**
A home-loan top-up is usually cheaper, because it is secured by the same property. A car or personal loan top-up is priced like a personal loan.

**Is the interest on a home-loan top-up tax deductible?**
Only if the money is used to buy, build or renovate a house, with proof. Otherwise there is no tax benefit.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — General Eligibility Policy — Overview

> This is a fictional demo policy of "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. It does not describe a real bank's policy.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — General Eligibility Policy — General Eligibility Principles

LoanMate evaluates a new loan application primarily using the Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio (FOIR) — the proportion of a customer's monthly income already committed to existing loan EMIs plus the proposed new EMI.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — General Eligibility Policy — FOIR Guidance

In this demo policy:

- FOIR up to 50% of monthly income: generally eligible
- FOIR between 50% and 60%: possibly eligible, subject to further review
- FOIR above 60%: generally not eligible for the requested amount

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — General Eligibility Policy — Credit Score

A credit score of 700 or above is generally preferred across LoanMate products. Applicants with a lower score may still be considered but are more likely to be offered a higher interest rate or a smaller loan amount.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — General Eligibility Policy — Section: Income Requirements by Product

| Product | Minimum monthly income (salaried) |
|---|---|
| Personal Loan | ₹25,000 |
| Home Loan | ₹30,000 |
| Vehicle Loan | ₹20,000 |

Self-employed applicants are generally assessed on annual income and business vintage instead of monthly salary.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — General Eligibility Policy — Section: Age and Employment

Most LoanMate products require the applicant to be between 21 and 65 years old at loan maturity, and to be salaried, self-employed, or (for home loans) an NRI, with a minimum period of employment or business operation as specified for each product.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — General Eligibility Policy — Frequently Asked Questions

**How is loan eligibility actually calculated for a new loan?**
LoanMate's demo eligibility check estimates the EMI for the requested loan amount and tenure, adds it to any existing EMI obligations, and compares the total against the applicant's monthly income to compute FOIR, as described above.

**Is this a guaranteed approval?**
No. This is a preliminary, automated estimate for demonstration purposes only, not a final underwriting decision.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Foreclosure Policy — Overview

> This is a fictional demo policy of "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. It does not describe a real bank's policy.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Foreclosure Policy — What Is Foreclosure

Foreclosure means paying off your entire remaining loan balance in one lump sum, closing the loan completely before its original scheduled end date. This is different from a partial prepayment, which only reduces the balance without closing the loan.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Foreclosure Policy — Eligibility for Foreclosure

Floating-rate loans taken by individuals can be foreclosed at any time, with no lock-in period, as required by RBI rules. For fixed-rate loans, foreclosure is allowed after a minimum lock-in period, which varies by loan type:

- Personal Loan: after 12 EMIs
- Home Loan: after 6 EMIs
- Vehicle Loan: after 12 EMIs
- Education Loan: after the moratorium period ends and at least 6 EMIs have been paid
- Business Loan: after 12 EMIs

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Foreclosure Policy — Foreclosure Charges

Floating-rate loans taken by individuals carry no foreclosure charge — RBI rules prohibit it. For fixed-rate loans, a foreclosure charge of 2% to 5% of the outstanding principal may apply, at the rate stated in the loan's Key Fact Statement.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Foreclosure Policy — Section: Process

To foreclose a loan, a customer should:

1. Request a foreclosure quote, which shows the exact payoff amount as of a chosen date.
2. Make the full payment by the specified date.
3. Receive a no-dues certificate and loan closure confirmation from LoanMate.
4. Collect the original property documents. Under RBI rules they must be returned, and any charge on the property removed, within 30 days of closure — or the bank pays ₹5,000 per day of delay.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Foreclosure Policy — Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the difference between prepayment and foreclosure?**
Prepayment is a partial extra payment that reduces your balance but keeps the loan open. Foreclosure is paying the entire remaining balance at once and closing the loan.

**Will foreclosure affect my credit score?**
Successfully foreclosing a loan is generally reported as "closed" and does not negatively affect your credit score; in fact, a clean closure history is typically viewed favourably.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Missed EMI Policy — Overview

> This is a fictional demo policy of "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. It does not describe a real bank's policy.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Missed EMI Policy — What Happens If You Miss an EMI

If an EMI payment is not received by its due date, LoanMate's demo policy is as follows:

1. A penal charge is levied (see the Charges section below).
2. The missed payment may be reported to credit bureaus, which can negatively affect the customer's credit score.
3. LoanMate will attempt to contact the customer to understand the reason for the missed payment and discuss options.

metadata.section: What Happens If You Miss an EMI

text:
LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Missed EMI Policy — Section: Charges

A penal charge of 2% of the missed EMI amount, or ₹500, whichever is higher, applies per missed EMI in this demo policy. As required by RBI rules, this is a fixed penal charge — it is not added to the loan's interest rate, and no interest is charged on it. If an auto-debit (NACH) mandate fails for lack of funds, a bounce charge of ₹500 plus GST also applies.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Missed EMI Policy — Grace Period

LoanMate's demo policy allows a grace period of 3 days from the due date before a payment is formally marked as "missed" and the late fee is applied. Payments made within this grace period are not treated as late.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Missed EMI Policy — Section: Repeated Missed Payments

Any overdue EMI is reported to credit bureaus: under RBI rules the loan is flagged SMA-0 when overdue up to 30 days, SMA-1 at 31–60 days and SMA-2 at 61–90 days, and becomes a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) once overdue for more than 90 days. LoanMate may then initiate a formal recovery process, always following RBI's fair recovery rules — no harassment, and no recovery calls before 8 a.m. or after 7 p.m. Customers experiencing financial difficulty are strongly encouraged to contact LoanMate proactively before missing a payment, as restructuring or a revised repayment plan may be possible.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Missed EMI Policy — Frequently Asked Questions

**What should I do if I know I will miss an upcoming EMI?**
Contact LoanMate as early as possible. Proactively flagging a payment difficulty gives more options for resolution than a payment that is simply missed without notice.

**Does a single missed EMI close my loan?**
No. A single missed EMI results in a late fee and a potential credit score impact, but does not close the loan. Loan status changes to "Overdue" when payments remain unpaid, and to NPA after more than 90 days overdue, as described above.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Prepayment Policy — Overview

> This is a fictional demo policy of "LoanMate Bank," created for the LoanMate AI academic project. It does not describe a real bank's policy.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Prepayment Policy — What Is Prepayment

Prepayment means paying an extra lump-sum amount towards your loan's outstanding principal, in addition to your regular EMIs. Prepayment reduces the outstanding balance, which in turn reduces either your future EMI amount or your remaining tenure, depending on the option you choose.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Prepayment Policy — When Prepayment Is Allowed

Floating-rate loans taken by individuals can be prepaid at any time, with no lock-in period, as required by RBI rules. Fixed-rate loans can be prepaid after a minimum of 12 EMIs have been paid in this demo policy.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Prepayment Policy — Prepayment Charges

Floating-rate loans taken by individuals carry no prepayment or foreclosure charges at all — this is an RBI rule that applies to every bank in India (see the RBI prepayment rules document). Fixed-rate loans may carry a prepayment charge of 2% to 5% of the outstanding principal, depending on the loan product; the exact charge is stated in the loan's Key Fact Statement, and no undisclosed charge can be levied.

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Prepayment Policy — How Prepayment Affects Your Loan

When you make a prepayment, LoanMate recalculates your loan using your original interest rate and remaining tenure, applied to the new, lower outstanding balance. In the standard LoanMate demo calculation, the remaining tenure is kept the same and the EMI amount is reduced. (Note: some real-world lenders instead offer to keep the EMI the same and reduce the tenure — always confirm which option applies to your actual loan.)

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Prepayment Policy — Section: Charges

| Loan type | Typical prepayment charge |
|---|---|
| Any floating-rate loan to an individual (home, personal, education, etc.) | Nil — RBI rule |
| Floating-rate business loan to an individual or micro/small enterprise | Nil — RBI rule (loans sanctioned from 1 January 2026) |
| Personal Loan (fixed rate) | 2% – 5% of outstanding principal |
| Home Loan (fixed rate) | 2% of outstanding principal |
| Vehicle Loan (fixed rate) | Up to 5% in the first year, up to 3% after |
| Business Loan (fixed rate) | 2% – 4% of outstanding principal |

LoanMate Bank (Demo) — Prepayment Policy — Frequently Asked Questions

**Is there a minimum prepayment amount?**
LoanMate does not enforce a minimum prepayment amount in this demo policy, but very small prepayments may not meaningfully change your EMI.

**Can I prepay multiple times?**
Yes, prepayment can be made more than once during the loan tenure, subject, for fixed-rate loans, to the 12-EMI waiting period being met at least once.

RBI Rules for Digital Loans and Loan Apps (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of the RBI guidelines on digital lending (September 2022), consolidated into the RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025. Applies to all banks and regulated lenders in India. General information, not legal advice. Last reviewed: October 2026.

RBI Rules for Digital Loans and Loan Apps (Public Information) — Money Flows Only Between You and the Lender

For any loan taken through an app or website, the loan must be paid directly into the borrower's own bank account, and repayments must go directly into the regulated lender's account. A loan app or agent (Lending Service Provider) cannot route the money through its own or a third party's account. Any fees payable to the app must be paid by the lender, not charged directly to the borrower.

metadata.section: Money Flows Only Between You and the Lender

text:
RBI Rules for Digital Loans and Loan Apps (Public Information) — Key Fact Statement and Cooling-Off Period

The borrower must get a Key Fact Statement with the all-in Annual Percentage Rate (APR) before signing. Digital loans must also offer a cooling-off (look-up) period — at least three days for loans with a tenure of seven days or more, and one day for shorter loans — during which the borrower can exit by repaying the principal and proportionate APR, without any penalty.

metadata.section: Key Fact Statement and Cooling-Off Period

text:
RBI Rules for Digital Loans and Loan Apps (Public Information) — Data and Phone Access

Lending apps may collect only the data needed for the loan, with the borrower's explicit consent. They must not access the phone's contact list, photos, media files or call logs (one-time access for KYC to camera, microphone and location is allowed with consent).

RBI Rules for Digital Loans and Loan Apps (Public Information) — Check the App Is Genuine

Every regulated lender must publish the list of digital lending apps and partners it works with on its website, and the RBI maintains a public directory of digital lending apps of regulated entities on its website. Loan apps not linked to a bank or RBI-registered NBFC are illegal and are a common source of harassment and fraud.

RBI Rules for Digital Loans and Loan Apps (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**A loan app is threatening to message my contacts. What should I do?**
Genuine regulated lenders cannot access your contacts or harass you. Report the app at cybercrime.gov.in or by calling 1930, and complain to the lender and the RBI Ombudsman if the lender is regulated.

Return of Property Documents After Loan Closure (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of the RBI circular "Responsible Lending Conduct – Release of Movable / Immovable Property Documents on Repayment / Settlement of Personal Loans" (13 September 2023, effective 1 December 2023). Applies to all banks and regulated lenders in India. General information, not legal advice. Last reviewed: October 2026.

Return of Property Documents After Loan Closure (Public Information) — 30-Day Deadline

After a borrower fully repays or settles a loan, the lender must return all original movable and immovable property documents (for example, the sale deed of a house or the registration papers of a vehicle) and remove any charge registered with a registry, within 30 days.

Return of Property Documents After Loan Closure (Public Information) — Where to Collect

The borrower can choose to collect the original documents either from the branch where the loan account was serviced or from any other office of the lender where the documents are kept. The place and timeline for returning documents must be stated in the sanction letter.

Return of Property Documents After Loan Closure (Public Information) — Compensation for Delay

If the lender delays returning the documents or removing the charge beyond 30 days for reasons attributable to the lender, it must tell the borrower the reasons and pay compensation of ₹5,000 for each day of delay.

Return of Property Documents After Loan Closure (Public Information) — Lost or Damaged Documents

If original documents are lost or damaged while with the lender, the lender must help the borrower get duplicate or certified copies and bear all the costs, in addition to the compensation. The lender gets an extra 30 days for this (60 days in total); the ₹5,000-per-day compensation applies after that.

Return of Property Documents After Loan Closure (Public Information) — Death of the Borrower

Lenders must have a clear, published procedure for returning original documents to the legal heirs if the sole or joint borrower dies.

Return of Property Documents After Loan Closure (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**I closed my home loan. What should I collect from the bank?**
The original property documents, a no-dues or loan closure certificate, and confirmation that the bank's charge on the property has been removed (for example, from CERSAI).

Floating Interest Rates, Repo-Linked Loans and EMI Reset (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of RBI rules on external benchmark lending (circular of 4 September 2019) and the RBI circular "Reset of Floating Interest Rate on EMI based Personal Loans" (18 August 2023). Applies to all banks in India. General information, not legal advice. Last reviewed: October 2026.

Floating Interest Rates, Repo-Linked Loans and EMI Reset (Public Information) — External Benchmark Linked Rate (EBLR)

Since 1 October 2019, every new floating-rate retail loan (home, personal, vehicle, education) and MSME loan from a bank must be linked to an external benchmark — usually the RBI's repo rate, or a government Treasury Bill yield published by FBIL. The bank adds a spread on top of the benchmark. The rate must be reset at least once every three months, so when the RBI changes the repo rate, the borrower's rate follows at the next reset.

Floating Interest Rates, Repo-Linked Loans and EMI Reset (Public Information) — Older Benchmarks: MCLR and Base Rate

Loans taken earlier may still be linked to the bank's Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR, introduced April 2016) or the older Base Rate. These internal benchmarks pass on RBI rate changes more slowly. Borrowers on MCLR or Base Rate can ask their bank to switch to an EBLR-linked rate, usually for a nominal fee.

metadata.section: Older Benchmarks: MCLR and Base Rate

text:
Floating Interest Rates, Repo-Linked Loans and EMI Reset (Public Information) — When a Floating Rate Changes — Borrower Options

Under the RBI's 2023 rules, when a floating rate is reset the bank must clearly inform the borrower and offer a choice: increase the EMI, extend the tenure, or a mix of both; prepay part or all of the loan at any time; or switch to a fixed rate as per the bank's policy (any switching charge must be disclosed). The tenure cannot be extended so far that the EMI no longer covers the interest (negative amortisation).

metadata.section: When a Floating Rate Changes — Borrower Options

text:
Floating Interest Rates, Repo-Linked Loans and EMI Reset (Public Information) — Quarterly Loan Statement

Banks must give borrowers of EMI-based floating-rate loans a statement at least every quarter showing the principal and interest paid so far, the EMI amount, the number of EMIs left, and the annualised interest rate for the full tenure.

Floating Interest Rates, Repo-Linked Loans and EMI Reset (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**The RBI cut the repo rate. When will my EMI fall?**
For a repo-linked loan, at the next reset date, which comes at least once every three months. Many banks reduce the tenure rather than the EMI by default — you can ask the bank to reduce the EMI instead.

**Can I switch from a floating rate to a fixed rate?**
Yes, banks must offer the option at reset as per their board-approved policy. Fixed rates are usually higher, and a switching fee may apply; it must be disclosed upfront.

Key Fact Statement (KFS) and Annual Percentage Rate (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of the RBI circular on Key Fact Statement for loans and advances (15 April 2024). Applies to all banks and regulated lenders in India. General information, not legal advice — check rbi.org.in for the current text. Last reviewed: October 2026.

Key Fact Statement (KFS) and Annual Percentage Rate (Public Information) — What Is a Key Fact Statement

A Key Fact Statement (KFS) is a short, standard-format summary of a loan's key terms that the lender must give the borrower before the loan agreement is signed. Since 1 October 2024, a KFS is mandatory for all retail and MSME term loans, including home, personal, vehicle and education loans. It must be in a language the borrower understands.

metadata.section: What Is a Key Fact Statement

text:
Key Fact Statement (KFS) and Annual Percentage Rate (Public Information) — What the KFS Shows

The KFS lists the loan amount, tenure, interest rate and type (fixed or floating), the EMI and repayment schedule, all fees and charges (processing fee, insurance, legal or valuation charges), penal charges, prepayment or foreclosure charges, the cooling-off period for digital loans, and the lender's grievance redressal contact.

Key Fact Statement (KFS) and Annual Percentage Rate (Public Information) — Annual Percentage Rate (APR)

The KFS must show the Annual Percentage Rate (APR) — the all-in annual cost of the loan, including the interest rate and all fees and charges paid to the lender. The APR is the best single number for comparing loans from different lenders, because a loan with a lower interest rate but high fees can cost more overall.

Key Fact Statement (KFS) and Annual Percentage Rate (Public Information) — Charges Not in the KFS

Any fee or charge that is not mentioned in the KFS cannot be charged to the borrower at any point during the loan's life without the borrower's explicit consent.

Key Fact Statement (KFS) and Annual Percentage Rate (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**How long do I get to read the KFS?**
For loans with a tenure of seven days or more, the KFS must stay valid for at least three working days, so the borrower can compare and decide without pressure.

**Is the APR the same as the interest rate?**
No. The interest rate is only the cost of borrowing the money. The APR also includes fees and charges, so it is usually higher than the interest rate.

KYC (Know Your Customer) Rules for Bank Customers (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of the RBI Master Direction – Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, as amended. Applies to all banks in India. General information, not legal advice. Last reviewed: October 2026.

KYC (Know Your Customer) Rules for Bank Customers (Public Information) — Why Banks Need KYC

RBI rules require every bank to verify the identity and address of its customers and to keep that information up to date. If KYC is not updated when due, the bank may restrict some operations on the account until it is completed.

KYC (Know Your Customer) Rules for Bank Customers (Public Information) — Officially Valid Documents (OVDs)

Any one of these can be used as proof of identity and address: passport, driving licence, proof of possession of Aadhaar number, Voter ID card, NREGA job card signed by a State Government officer, or a letter from the National Population Register. A PAN card (or Form 60 if the customer has no PAN) is also required. If the address on the document is not current, other documents such as a recent utility bill can be used as deemed proof of address for a limited time.

KYC (Know Your Customer) Rules for Bank Customers (Public Information) — Periodic KYC Update

Banks must periodically update KYC based on the customer's risk category: at least once every 2 years for high-risk, every 8 years for medium-risk, and every 10 years for low-risk customers. If nothing has changed, a customer can usually update KYC with a simple self-declaration through email, registered mobile, net banking, ATM, or a letter — without visiting the branch.

KYC (Know Your Customer) Rules for Bank Customers (Public Information) — Ways to Complete KYC

KYC can be completed at any branch, through Aadhaar-based e-KYC, or through Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP, or video KYC), where a bank official verifies the customer over a live video call through the bank's official app or website. Central KYC (CKYC) gives each customer a KYC Identifier Number (KIN) that can be reused across banks.

KYC (Know Your Customer) Rules for Bank Customers (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**Someone called saying my KYC will expire and asked for my OTP. Is that the bank?**
No. Banks never ask for an OTP, PIN, password or full card details over a call, SMS or link. That is a KYC fraud — do not share anything, and report it to the cyber fraud helpline 1930.

**Is Aadhaar compulsory for KYC?**
No. Aadhaar is one of several officially valid documents; a customer can use a passport, driving licence, Voter ID or the other listed documents instead.

RBI Rules on Penal Charges for Late Payment (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of the RBI circular "Fair Lending Practice – Penal Charges in Loan Accounts" (RBI/2023-24/53, 18 August 2023). Applies to all banks and NBFCs in India. General information, not legal advice — check rbi.org.in for the current text. Last reviewed: October 2026.

RBI Rules on Penal Charges for Late Payment (Public Information) — Penal Charges, Not Penal Interest

When a borrower misses an EMI or breaks a material term of the loan, a lender may levy a penalty — but only as a fixed "penal charge". It cannot be added as extra "penal interest" on top of the loan's interest rate. This rule applies to fresh loans from 1 April 2024, and existing loans had to be moved to it by 30 June 2024.

RBI Rules on Penal Charges for Late Payment (Public Information) — No Interest on Penal Charges

Penal charges cannot be capitalised. That means no interest is charged on the penal charge itself — it does not compound. Normal interest on the overdue EMI amount continues as per the loan agreement.

RBI Rules on Penal Charges for Late Payment (Public Information) — Reasonable and Disclosed

There is no fixed upper limit, but penal charges must be reasonable and in proportion to the default, and the same for all borrowers in a loan or product category. Penal charges for individuals cannot be higher than those for non-individual borrowers for similar non-compliance. The amount and the reason must be disclosed in the loan agreement and Key Fact Statement, shown on the lender's website, and communicated to the borrower whenever a reminder for the breach is sent.

RBI Rules on Penal Charges for Late Payment (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**My bank added 2% penal interest to my loan rate after a missed EMI. Is that allowed?**
Not for loans covered by the 2023 RBI circular. A late payment penalty must be a separate penal charge, not an increase in the interest rate. You can raise a complaint with the bank and, if it is not resolved, with the RBI Ombudsman.

**Do penal charges apply to credit cards?**
No. Credit cards, external commercial borrowings, trade credits and structured obligations are covered by their own product-specific rules, not this circular.

RBI Rules on Prepayment and Foreclosure Charges (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rules that apply to all banks in India. Sources: RBI circular on foreclosure charges on floating-rate term loans (May 2012) and the RBI (Pre-payment Charges on Loans) Directions, 2025 (issued 2 July 2025). General information, not legal advice — check rbi.org.in for the current text. Last reviewed: October 2026.

RBI Rules on Prepayment and Foreclosure Charges (Public Information) — Floating-Rate Loans to Individuals — No Prepayment Charges

Since 2012, banks in India are not allowed to charge any foreclosure charge or prepayment penalty on floating-rate term loans given to individual borrowers. This covers most floating-rate home loans. A borrower can prepay part of the loan or close it fully at any time without a penalty.

RBI Rules on Prepayment and Foreclosure Charges (Public Information) — RBI Pre-payment Charges Directions, 2025

For loans sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 January 2026, the RBI's 2025 directions say:

- No prepayment charges on any floating-rate loan given to an individual for a non-business purpose, with or without co-borrowers.
- No prepayment charges on floating-rate loans for business purposes given to individuals and micro and small enterprises (MSEs) by commercial banks (other than small finance banks, regional rural banks and local area banks), Tier 4 urban co-operative banks, upper-layer NBFCs and all-India financial institutions.
- Small finance banks, regional rural banks, Tier 3 urban co-operative banks, state and central co-operative banks and middle-layer NBFCs cannot charge prepayment charges on such business loans up to ₹50 lakh.
- The rule applies whatever the source of the money used to prepay, and no minimum lock-in period can be imposed.

RBI Rules on Prepayment and Foreclosure Charges (Public Information) — Fixed-Rate and Other Loans

Prepayment or foreclosure charges may still apply to fixed-rate loans and loans outside the categories above. Any such charge must be disclosed upfront in the loan's Key Fact Statement (KFS) and sanction letter; a lender cannot levy a charge that was not disclosed. For hybrid (fixed-then-floating) loans, the no-charge rule applies if the loan is on a floating rate when it is prepaid.

RBI Rules on Prepayment and Foreclosure Charges (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**Can my bank charge me for closing my floating-rate home loan early?**
No. For individual borrowers, floating-rate loans cannot carry foreclosure or prepayment charges under RBI rules.

**I took a fixed-rate personal loan. Can there be a prepayment charge?**
Yes, fixed-rate loans can carry a prepayment charge, but only at the rate disclosed in your Key Fact Statement and loan agreement.

**Does it matter whether I prepay with my own savings or a loan from another bank (balance transfer)?**
No. Under the 2025 directions, the no-charge rule applies regardless of the source of funds.

Overdue Loans, NPA Classification and Fair Recovery Practices (Public Information) — Overview

> Public information: a plain-language summary of RBI rules on asset classification (Prudential norms, including the clarification of 12 November 2021) and on conduct of recovery agents (circular of 12 August 2022). Applies to all banks in India. General information, not legal advice. Last reviewed: October 2026.

Overdue Loans, NPA Classification and Fair Recovery Practices (Public Information) — Special Mention Accounts (SMA)

Banks flag a loan as soon as an EMI is overdue, in stages: SMA-0 when it is overdue for up to 30 days, SMA-1 for 31 to 60 days, and SMA-2 for 61 to 90 days. These stages are reported to credit bureaus and can lower the borrower's credit score.

Overdue Loans, NPA Classification and Fair Recovery Practices (Public Information) — Non-Performing Asset (NPA)

A loan becomes a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) when principal or interest stays overdue for more than 90 days. An NPA account is upgraded back to "standard" only when the entire overdue amount — all arrears of interest and principal — is paid; paying just one EMI is not enough.

Overdue Loans, NPA Classification and Fair Recovery Practices (Public Information) — Fair Recovery Practices

Banks and their recovery agents must not use intimidation or harassment of any kind, verbal or physical. They must not call borrowers before 8 a.m. or after 7 p.m. for recovery. They must not publicly humiliate the borrower, intrude on the privacy of family members, friends or colleagues, send inappropriate messages, or make threatening or anonymous calls. A bank is responsible for the conduct of the recovery agents it hires.

Overdue Loans, NPA Classification and Fair Recovery Practices (Public Information) — Restructuring and Talking to the Bank Early

Borrowers facing genuine financial difficulty should contact their bank before missing EMIs. Banks can, as per their board policy, consider options such as rescheduling EMIs, extending the tenure, or restructuring the loan. A restructured loan may be reported as such to credit bureaus.

Overdue Loans, NPA Classification and Fair Recovery Practices (Public Information) — Frequently Asked Questions

**A recovery agent called me at 10 p.m. and threatened me. What can I do?**
That breaks RBI rules. Note the date, time and number, complain to the bank in writing, and if the bank does not resolve it within 30 days, complain to the RBI Ombudsman. Threats can also be reported to the police.

**After how many missed EMIs does a loan become an NPA?**
When any amount stays overdue for more than 90 days — roughly three missed EMIs in a row.
